conventions.convention: Fields are real L² equivalence classes; curl is distributional. H₀(curl;Ω) is the H(curl) graph closure of compactly supported smooth vector fields, without an assumed trace-kernel identification.
Ω is a nonempty bounded Lipschitz polyhedron with a finite matching affine tetrahedral mesh. Edge circulations and face fluxes use chosen global orientations and cellwise polynomial representatives.

The PEC electric space is V_h=N_h¹∩H₀(curl), the scalar space is S_h=W_h⁰∩H₀¹, and the magnetic space is the full face space N_h². The coordinate maps satisfy DC=CG=0; D denotes magnetic face-to-cell incidence.

Material tensors are measurable, essentially bounded, symmetric, static and uniformly positive; conductivity is symmetric nonnegative. SI coefficient units are retained, and H_h=μ⁻¹B_h is required only to lie in L².
The coercive form has the positive sign +s²ε with real s>0. Its graph norm uses a fixed reference length ℓ₀>0; the refining mesh family is shape regular.

Absolute harmonic dimensions refer to the full Whitney complex. PEC-relative harmonic complements are separate spaces; their dimensions are not identified with the absolute Betti numbers. Orthogonality is unweighted real L².
Countable Choice is explicit for the graph-space, energy and coercive arguments. The relative compactness and quotient-Poincaré clause additionally assumes full AC, including CC and DC.
The resonance example uses m,n≥1, a,b,d>0, constant scalar ε,μ>0, β=0, and ω_mn=k_mn/√(εμ); its real-frequency form has the negative sign −ω_mn²ε.

load_bearing.statement: For the stated PEC Whitney spaces, static positive material tensors, nonnegative conductivity and continuous current load, the weak Galerkin equations are exactly M_e dot e=CᵀM_b b−Se−j and dot b=−Ce, with symmetric positive-definite mass matrices, symmetric positive-semidefinite S, and DC=CG=0. Zero-dimensional basis spaces are allowed.

Under Countable Choice, the stated bounded Lipschitz domain, static uniformly positive symmetric coefficients, real s>0, fixed ℓ₀>0, bounded real linear F, and shape-regular refining matching tetrahedral meshes, the positive-shift variational problem and every conforming Galerkin problem have unique solutions. With α=min{(b_μℓ₀²)⁻¹,s²a_ε} and M=max{(a_μℓ₀²)⁻¹,s²b_ε}, ||u−u_n||_{V,ℓ₀}≤(M/α) inf_{v_n∈V_n}||u−v_n||_{V,ℓ₀}, and u_n→u in that norm.

alerts.finding: In the published supplier's Proof, step 5.1 says “Steps 1.1–2.2 therefore show”, and step 6.1 says “by steps 3.1–2.2”. There is no step 2.2: the proof has steps 1.1, 2.1, 3.1, 4.1, 5.1 and 6.1. The needed cochain identification and duality are available in steps 3.1–4.1, so these are broken internal references rather than a mathematical counterexample.

seams_checked.note: Compared the draft finite-system Definition and energy/existence theorem with the Whitney assembly and discrete-balance consumer. Matrix sizes, zero-dimensional conventions, signs, continuity of j, DC=CG=0 and q=−GᵀM_e e agree. The consumer proves load continuity and identifies its integral energy with the matrix energy.

Compared the draft finite-energy boundary Definition with the local semidiscretization and coercive theorem. Static measurable positive symmetric coefficients, SI units and closure-defined PEC space agree. The semidiscretization explicitly requires only L² magnetic intensity, and does not import continuum H(curl) regularity or an unsupported boundary trace.
